title: YouTube Video Redirect Service
subtitle: YouTube Video Link Handler
description: A small Flask app that uses yt-dlp to find a YouTube video’s direct media link and play it. For a shared song queue and OBS, see Streaming Player.
longDescription: A Flask service that accepts a video ID, resolves a direct media URL with yt-dlp and renders a player. The final version includes Docker and a JavaScript runtime for extraction. New song-request and OBS work continues in Streaming Player.
mascotLines: In 2026 it still finds the link, then Edge blocks the video. That was its one job.
YouTube doesn't refuse, it rations: about 15 lookups per 40 minutes.
imageCaptions: The 2021 version: the raw direct link printed above the player. Styling was optional.
Today's version: paste a link, the file plays, and the direct link sits under it
features: Direct media URL resolution with yt-dlp
results: Runnable final version preserved with tests and Docker
why: The 2021 question was simple: where does a YouTube video actually live? Behind each watch page sits a plain file on Google's servers, youtube-dl could find it, and the idea came from zdwolfe/yt-redirector. In 2026 the link still comes back; whether the video plays depends on what YouTube changed that week.
gains: Handy for seeing what yt-dlp actually returns for a page: the direct file link, title and type, above a plain player that recommends nothing afterwards. In the November 2026 tests YouTube stopped at the link; Wikimedia Commons pages still played end to end.
lessons: On 2026-11-04 yt-dlp still found the googlevideo.com link, but Edge blocked YouTube's reply as ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB, the one step this app exists for.
YouTube rations links rather than refusing them: after about fifteen lookups in forty minutes it asked for a bot check; half an hour later they came back.
The format is "best" because a plain <video> tag cannot join separate video and audio streams, so only single-file formats qualify.
